data.name: Shrivan
data.gender_notes: Shrivan is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Shri is the Goddess of wealth, prosperity and abundance. Van is a prefix meaning 'forest' or 'abode'. Together, Shrivan can be interpreted as the 'God of the abundant forest' or the 'God of the prosperous abode'. The name Shrivan carries the meaning “God of abundance and prosperity” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit. Parents who choose Shrivan usually hope their child will grow to embody god of abundance and prosperity and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Shrivan is a name of reverence for the divine, symbolizing the abundance and prosperity that comes from a connection to nature and the universe.
data.etymology: Shrivan belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of abundance and prosperity.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Shrivan total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: The name Shrivan may reflect Indian cultural traditions associating deities with abundant natural resources, such as forests. This name could also symbolize wealth and prosperity within the community, as the name directly includes the invocation to Shri, the Goddess associated with wealth and abundance.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu tradition, Shrivan may be seen as a spiritual symbol of the abundant and thriving natural world, representing the bountiful gifts of nature that sustain all life. It also underscores the spiritual significance of recognizing and expressing gratitude for the material blessings and abundance in our lives. The name evokes a sense of connection to the Divine as the provider of all sustenance.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Shrivan, the name of a Hindu deity, symbolizes the embodiment of wisdom and humility. The prefix 'Shri' denotes abundance and divine grace, while 'Van' represents the forest of knowledge, symbolizing one's continuous pursuit of wisdom and self-realization.

historical_references.reference: Shrivan was an important general in the army of the Chalukya king, Pulakeshin II, during the 7th century. He is best known for his victory over the Pallava king, Narasimhavarman II, in the Battle of Thothikonda.

Shrivan is also mentioned in the epic poem, the Mahabharata, as the son of Bhishma Pitamaha and Veda Prabha. He is described as a mighty warrior and one of the twelve Vasus, powerful deities who personify various natural elements.
